source.title: Security forces kill 12 India-sponsored terrorists in multiple IBOs in Balochistan: ISPR
source.summary: Security forces killed 12 India-sponsored terrorists in four separate intelligence-based operations (IBOs) in Balochistan between November 20 and 23, the military’s media wing said on Thursday. According to the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR), security forces targeted a terrorist hideout in Nushki district on November 20. Following an intense exchange of fire, eight terrorists belonging to the Indian-backed Fitna-al-Hindustan were killed. Weapons and ammunition were also recovered from the site, the ISPR added. The state has designated Balochistan-based terrorist groups as Fitna-al-Hindustan to highlight India’s alleged role in terrorism and destabilisation across Pakistan. On November 21, security forces intercepted the movement of terrorists in Sibi district, killing two more, the ISPR said. In two separate engagements in Panjgur and Kech districts on November 22 and 23, security forces raided terrorist hideouts and killed two more terrorists belonging to Fitna-al-Hindustan , the ISPR added. source.title: MNA among senior JUI-F leaders detained in Sargodha: police
source.summary: Several senior Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F) leaders were detained in Sargodha late on Wednesday, police said, prompting the party to demand their “immediate release”. The developments come amid tensions between Fazl and the federal government, which have been ongoing since mid-October. Sargodha Regional Police Officer (RPO) Sohail Sukhera told Dawn that Maulana Abdul Ghafoor Haideri, a member of the National Assembly, Malik Awais and Maulana Amjad Khan were detained at a house in Sargodha and served notices for violating Section 144 imposed across the division. He added that several other party leaders had also been arrested. Responding to a question about Maulana Haideri’s arrest, Sukhera said the leaders had not been arrested but that “their movement had been restricted in the division”. In a post on X last night, JUI-F claimed that Punjab police had “arrested” MNA Haideri, Maulana Khan and Awais. “The government should come to its senses; if they are not released immediately, the Punjab government will be held responsible for the consequences,” the post quoted party spokesperson Aslam Ghouri as saying.
